item.title: Tunisia NGO slams 'inhumane' prison conditions after dozens of detainee deaths
item.description:
Tunisia's main rights group on Friday denounced "inhumane" conditions in Tunisian prisons, saying 30 inmates have died since the beginning of summer, the country's hottest on record.

Authorities have yet to release figures for prison deaths after a summer marked by multiple heatwaves, water shortages and power cuts.

"The situation in prisons is inhumane and catastrophic," said Bassem Trifi, head of the Tunisian League for Human Rights, adding that "overcrowding and the lack of healthcare" in prisons were a major issue.

item.title: UN refugee agency seeks $7.1 bn in 2027
item.description:
The United Nations' refugee agency said on Friday it was seeking a much-reduced $7.1 billion to protect stateless people and respond to emergencies in 2027.

UNHCR chief Barham Salih warned last month that his agency was being "asked to do the impossible", over-stretched by a huge funding shortfall and near record-high population displacements around the world.

UNHCR's 2026 appeal targeted $8.5 billion -- of which only $2.9 billion has been raised to date.

item.title: OPEC+ expected to hold Q1 2027 output steady amid disputes
item.description: OPEC+ is conducting its first-ever review of members' production capacity to guide 2027 output targets and prevent the kind of quota disputes that have driven some countries to leave the cartel.

item.title: War, fear drive Sudanese writer Baraka Sakin's fiction
item.description:
A lifetime of war and persecution has shaped the writing of Sudanese novelist Abdelaziz Baraka Sakin, who has turned the fear and longing that are so central to his experience into his main drive.

The 63-year-old fled Sudan for Europe in 2012 and then returned, dreaming of an end to his forced exile.

But the war that erupted in 2023 and killed more than 200,000 people pushed him out again.

Still, he keeps writing.

item.title: UN urges Costa Rica to let in Palestinians rapporteur
item.description:
The United Nations on Friday urged Costa Rica to urgently reconsider its ban on admitting the UN special rapporteur on Palestinian rights and let her into the country.

Costa Rica's government said Thursday it had denied entry to Francesca Albanese, who has accused Israel of genocide, because she was the subject of an "international alert over links to terrorist acts".

Italian lawyer Albanese is the UN special rapporteur on the situation of human rights in the Palestinian territory occupied since 1967.

item.title: Funding cuts force mass closures of shelters for refugee women, UN says
item.description:
By Emma Farge

GENEVA, Nov 27 (Reuters) - Nearly half of shelters for displaced women and girls across over a dozen countries have closed since the beginning of last year due to funding cuts, leaving them more vulnerable to sexual abuse and violence, the UN refugee agency said on Friday.

These safe spaces help survivors of war orabduction to seek psychological support and other services while protecting them from rape and abuse in camps where ill-lit, crowded conditions canincrease risks.

item.title: Trump backs Iraqi leader's efforts to assert more state authority
item.description:
Nov 27 (Reuters) - US President Donald Trump on Friday backed the Iraqi leader's drive to assert state control, including stopping the smuggling of Iraqi oil, moves that put Baghdad in direct confrontation with Iran's militia allies and Kurdish authorities.

"We support Iraqi Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi’s efforts to assert state authority throughout Iraq, stop the smuggling of Iraqi oil, end corruption, and bring all weapons under the exclusive control of the state," Trump said in a Truth Social post.

item.description: Turkey called for a full investigation and legal action over what it described as “disproportionate” police force against the Turkish team’s fans during a match against Hapoel Beer-Sheva where 16 Turkish supporters were detained and later released.

item.title: Under-attack Palestinians find unlikely ally in Israeli retired general
item.description:
The four Israeli soldiers stepped out of their car in the occupied West Bank, their faces masked, their uniforms unmarked and automatic weapons strapped across their shoulders. 

They had entered a Palestinian olive grove but, little did they expect, the person there planning to tell them to leave could have once been issuing them orders.

A retired Israeli general, Eyal Ben Reuven, had come that day to the Palestinian town of As Sawiyah, on a mission to prevent some of the rampant violence against Palestinians by extremist Israeli settlers.

item.title: UN warns famine risks rising as hunger hotspots increase
item.description:
By Clara Schoenthaler

ROME, Nov 27 (Reuters) - Hunger is set to worsen significantly in 16 global hotspots over the coming six months, with famine threatening parts of Africa, two United Nations agencies warned on Friday.

The Food and Agriculture Organization (FAO) and World Food Programme (WFP) said Sudan, South Sudan, Somalia, northern Nigeria and Yemen faced the gravest threats, driven by conflict, displacement, economic hardship and extreme weather.

item.title: Exclusive-US pushed Venezuela, Iraq to consider leaving OPEC, sources say
item.description:
By Ahmad Ghaddar, Ahmed Rasheed and Marianna Parraga

LONDON/BAGHDAD/HOUSTON, Nov 27 (Reuters) - The Trump administration encouraged Venezuela and Iraq to consider leaving OPEC earlier this year and prevented Venezuela from paying its annual membership dues to the group, according to ten people familiar with the matter.

The previously unreported moves targeted two of OPEC's five founding members, marking an unusually direct challenge to an organization President Donald Trump has long accused of keeping oil prices artificially high.

item.title: Costa Rica bars entry to UN rapporteur over 'links to terrorist acts'
item.description:
Costa Rica's government said Thursday it had denied entry to UN rapporteur Francesca Albanese, who has accused Israel of genocide, because she was the subject of an "international alert over links to terrorist acts".

Albanese, the UN special rapporteur on the Palestinian territories, arrived Thursday at the airport serving the capital San Jose to receive an honorary degree from the University of Costa Rica, a public university.

item.title: Iran warns on Gulf military presence as South Korea readies expanded naval role
item.description:
SEOUL, Nov 27 (Reuters) - Iran's foreign minister has told his South Korean counterpart that a foreign military presence in the Gulf region would heighten tensions rather than contribute to peace, as Seoul prepares to expand the operational area of a navy unit to waters south of the Gulf of Oman.

Here are some details:

• Iran's Foreign Minister Abbas Araqchi spoke by telephone on Thursday with South Korea's Cho Hyun, who reaffirmed Seoul did not intend to join any war or deploy troops to the Gulf, the Iranian embassy in Seoul said in an X post on Friday.

item.title: Erdogan completes Turkey's ratification of Mecca defence pact
item.description:
ISTANBUL, Nov 27 (Reuters) - PresidentTayyip Erdogan has formally approved theMecca Joint Defence Agreement with Pakistan and Saudi Arabia, the Official Gazette said on Friday, completing Turkey'sratification after parliament ratifiedit earlier this month.

The three countries signed a joint defence agreement in Mecca in August amid escalating concerns about the increasingly aggressive US-Israeli war against Iran and they are scheduled to hold a meeting in Islamabad on Friday and Saturday.
